text:
ashley: Proposal: coalesce edge tiling and live fanout into a single "edge-coalesce" pipeline. Idea: for mixed dashboards, render static tiles at edge and stream live widgets, reducing backend fanout.

mei: Sounds promising. Main question: RBAC surface. Do auth at ingress and bake signed perm-version into tile keys?

rahul: Yes. Perm-version in tile key avoids serving stale tiles post-role-change. For hot role flips, we can tag tiles with owner-version to support targeted invalidation.

kevin: Cache key format suggestion: tenant:view:perm-v:tile-hash:bucket. Also include render-mode hint (coalesced|live) for observability.

maria: To limit auth volume, allow low-sensitivity tiles to be post-filtered while high-sensitivity require pre-auth. Product must annotate.

ashley: Routing rules: if estimated_render < 60ms and sensitivity!=high -> edge tile; else -> live fanout. Frontend may provide estimates or backend EWMA.

mei: Telemetry: tile_hit_rate, p95_edge, p95_live, auth_calls_per_view. Alert if p95_edge>300ms or tile_hit_rate drops >15% during rollout.

rahul: Rollout: feature flag edge-coalesce-v1, canary 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100%. Synthetic canary will compare HTML diffs and metrics.

sre-bot: Canary job started at 1770000100 for 400 synthetic dashboards. Will report mismatches to #incidents.

kevin: Security: perm-hash must be HMAC with rotation. Do not log unhashed perms.

maria: Perf note: precompile templates and warm top-k views at edge to avoid cold starts.

ashley: Action items: kevin draft RFC (API + cache keys), mei prototype invalidation workflow, rahul write canary harness, maria add sensitivity annotations. We'll reconvene after RFC.
